$comment: THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for every status claim in this repo.
Nothing else may carry one. ROADMAP.md §0b/§0c and docs/completion-tracker.html are
GENERATED from this file by `npm run status` — edit here, never there, or the next
generate silently reverts you. RESUME.md is untouched by the generator: it answers a
different question (how something was proved, and what it cost to find out) and is
append-only archaeology.
status  — proved:   a human has seen it work on the phone
partial:  works, with a named gap
untested: code and tests are in, no human has ever exercised it
broken:   works badly, defect logged in ROADMAP §2
none:     not built
blockedBy — what stands between this row and being finished. This is the field that
keeps the brain dependency visible rather than buried in prose, and it is
why the generator can say 'the app alone cannot reach 100%' with a number
instead of an opinion.
brain:     needs jarvis-brain — a gateway route, a merge, or a deploy
desk:      needs the desk machine on
device:    needs the phone in hand, unlocked (adb cannot unlock it)
app-build: app repo, but needs a native build or an EAS credentials action
app:       app repo, ships over the air
none:      finished, nothing owed

otaVerified.note: Runtime is byte-identical to the fingerprint the installed APK carries, so a JS-only publish reaches the phone. A LOCAL build still receives nothing unless the fingerprint is baked by hand.

brain.label: Brain
brain.detail: jarvis-brain — a gateway route, a merge, or a deploy. Deliberately not being touched; that repo is clean and fully pushed.

desk.label: Desk
desk.detail: Needs the desk machine on. This laptop has no Python — `python` opens the Microsoft Store.

device.label: Phone
device.detail: Needs the phone in hand and unlocked. `adb` can wake the display but cannot unlock it, so the app launches behind the keyguard and never foregrounds — `apps_linked: 0` in that state means nothing.

app-build.label: App · build
app-build.detail: App repo, but needs a native build or an EAS credentials action rather than an over-the-air publish.

app.label: App
app.detail: App repo, ships over the air. Nothing outside this repo is owed.

criteria.title: Every state names itself
criteria.detail: Already the rule, and the two live defects are both what happens when it slips. A silent failure in a security path is a security failure. One defect is fixed in the app; the other is fixed in the brain and undeployed.

criteria.title: No feature arrives twice or lies once
criteria.detail: The anti-duplicate gate is built and its decision carries tests; no departure window has run yet. The false Saturday remark is fixed in the brain as c86d176 and not deployed.

criteria.title: He can be reached without the app being opened
criteria.detail: Push is proved — it buzzed. Continuous presence needs BOOT_COMPLETED and the notification listener, and neither exists yet. The listener is itself gated by criterion 7.

criteria.title: He speaks and he listens
criteria.detail: The microphone has never been exercised — the oldest unverified thing here. Voice out is not built at all, and until both land this is a beautifully themed text box.

criteria.title: He knows where and when he is
criteria.detail: One field on the persona envelope, and it is a gateway change. The roadmap calls it the most character per line of code in the whole document.

criteria.title: Memory survives a deploy
criteria.detail: Rolling memory is in Postgres rather than RAM, but deploy-durable state is committed and undeployed. Render's disk goes on every deploy, and that has silently disarmed the briefing twice.

criteria.title: A compromised token does not expose a life
criteria.detail: One string still gates the socket, push, the commute route and app state alike, and nothing expires. A gate on the senses, not a follow-up: once data has been collected badly, no later fix un-collects it.

criteria.title: A crash is visible
criteria.detail: Shipping a fix within the hour is solved — the OTA channel is verified as of today. Seeing the crash at all is not: a crash is silent, and adb logcat on the one machine that built the APK is the only diagnosis.

criteria.title: A second device is possible
criteria.detail: Signed with Expo's debug keystore, which is why a local APK and an EAS-signed one cannot replace each other. Fine for one phone, not for the second.

criteria.title: It is usable by someone who cannot see it well
criteria.detail: Contrast is measured and passing at 4.78 and 4.68 against a 4.5 bar; reduced motion already defaults from the OS. Nothing has been checked with a screen reader.

rows.name: LAN probe → cloud fallback → WebSocket, reconnect
rows.note: One reducer serves every tab.

rows.name: One socket per launch; chat survives force-stop
Pairing token in SecureStore, with rotation
rows.note: New accepted, old refused 403.

rows.name: Biometric lock, re-locking on background
rows.note: `strong` only — Android rejects `BIOMETRIC_WEAK | DEVICE_CREDENTIAL` outright, and with a passcode fallback enabled no sheet appears and the promise never settles.

rows.name: Desk-key handshake (sealed turns)
rows.note: `has_desk_key: false`. 18 turns dropped and rising, so the encrypted path has never once worked end to end. Sealed-and-dropped is the correct failure and it is still a failure.

rows.name: `BRIDGE_SECRET` rotation
rows.note: The old value went through Render's access log before redaction landed and still opens `/desk-link`. A fake desk was connected with it repeatedly during testing. The only item whose cost grows while deferred.

rows.name: Capability-split tokens
rows.note: One string gates the socket, push, the commute route and app state alike. A token that can register a push and a token that can read your day must not be the same secret.

rows.name: Token expiry
rows.note: Nothing expires.

rows.name: Text chat, both directions
Replies arrive word by word
Markdown rendered, not shown as asterisks
Reasoning monologues can never reach the screen
rows.note: Proved in the harness, never on the device.

rows.name: The opening line is the real situation
rows.note: On-device, no model, no await.

rows.name: “What can you do”, answered without a round trip
rows.note: On-device, so it answers with everything even offline.

rows.name: A Capabilities screen listing the same thing
rows.note: One list, two surfaces. Read back over adb.

rows.name: A status panel naming every seam
rows.note: Eight rows, four states, assembled on the device so it is readable with nothing connected at all — which is exactly when it will be looked at. The briefing row was watched going red then green as the stamp landed. **The briefing row was refined 2026-08-24** to a third state, `CANNOT TELL`, so a stamp that has merely aged stops asserting the gateway lost the schedule; that state has 10 tests and no device pass yet.

rows.name: Whether the gateway holds a push address
rows.note: Nothing exposed this before, and it is the most diagnostic fact in the app.

rows.name: Photo preview and caption before sending
A photo answering with its own lookup marker
rows.note: Shared by the text and vision paths.

rows.name: A thumbnail in the chat instead of the word “Photo”
rows.note: A reply about a photo cannot be judged without the photo.

rows.name: Photo-in-flight indicator; a failed send stays recoverable
rows.note: The longest wait in the app, and the least visible.

rows.name: Sent / delivered / read ticks
rows.note: Only the gateway can say delivered and read, and it says neither. Needs a per-message id on both sides. The largest fully-specified thing left.

rows.name: Reply to a message
rows.note: Wants the same per-message id as the ticks, so it follows them rather than inventing a second identity for a message.

rows.name: Microphone in
rows.note: `brains.usage.audio` is 0. The oldest unverified thing here. If it reads `fell_back` with `last_error_was_quota: false` the mime is wrong — the phone records m4a and Google documents `audio/aac`, not `audio/mp4`.

rows.name: Voice out
rows.note: The largest single gap in the chat, and app-only — `expo-speech`.

rows.name: Push to a sleeping phone
rows.note: It buzzed. Reaches a dead app and is exempt from the background-execution block.

rows.name: Both notification channels exist on the device
rows.note: Confirmed by adb, neither deleted.

rows.name: The desk alert outranks an everyday one
rows.note: Importance 5 against 3.

rows.name: Renamed channels are deleted rather than left behind
rows.note: Six old channels all confirmed deleted. This app has renamed its everyday channel eight times, and every rename silently broke replies until the gateway was told.

rows.name: A notification tap opens Chat
A desk-watch alert reaching a closed app
rows.note: Tapping it opens the alert screen.

rows.name: A pushed departure briefing, unprompted
rows.note: It arrives. It also arrived twice — the gate is built but no departure window has run since.

rows.name: Briefing content, thresholds, quiet-day announcement
rows.note: Figures, never the model.

rows.name: He speaks first, once a day
rows.note: Fired for the first time and was wrong: a bare substring match let a Mon–Fri pattern assert a Saturday shift, and the prompt then asserted it as true today. Fixed in the brain as c86d176, not deployed. The same body also capitalised `Sir`, which the voice rule forbids.

rows.name: Briefings visible in the Activity panel
rows.note: They had been filtered out entirely.

rows.name: Read / unread per entry, surviving a restart
The local task gated so it cannot double-post
rows.note: The stamp works and carries 6 tests on the decision plus 3 on the wiring; the gate cases were checked by removing the gate and watching them go red. The duplicate itself cannot be checked until a departure window. Leave both unswiped and read the tags — a pushed one carries `tag=FCM-Notification:*`, a local post does not. The *display* half of the stamp's limitation is closed as of 2026-08-24: the panel no longer reads a stale stamp as the gateway having lost the schedule. The gate's own behaviour is unchanged and deliberately so — a stale stamp still means the phone posts.

rows.name: Full message on tap, day rules, paged list
rows.note: Shipped, and the box was collapsing to one line on the phone. Fixed and republished, awaiting a second look.

rows.name: Facts stored and recalled
rows.note: 14 facts known. Volunteered exactly once, wrongly.

rows.name: One assistant across desk, phone and chat
rows.note: App and chat share one history. A desk answering with its own brain bypasses it, so those turns never join the shared history.

rows.name: Rolling memory durable across restarts
rows.note: In Postgres, not RAM — the RAM claim was stale. Whether the shared-memory flag is actually on in Render's environment is unverified.

rows.name: Deploy-durable gateway state
rows.note: Committed on `fix/durable-state`, two commits ahead of the gateway branch, undeployed. Until it merges, every deploy silently disarms the briefing.

rows.name: Chat history sent with the ask
rows.note: The envelope carries one turn.

rows.name: Journal: usage source, rollup, fact sharing
rows.note: Derived facts only, never rows — the pattern every later sense copies.

rows.name: The journal’s denial path
rows.note: Reads “I cannot see your usage, sir — the permission is off.” Collected history stays visible under HELD ON THIS DEVICE, which is the honest distinction.

rows.name: Any background work running unattended
rows.note: **Cannot**, and measured twice rather than assumed: `expo-background-task` hardcodes `setRequiredNetworkType(CONNECTED)` and the uid reads `blocked=REASON_APP_BACKGROUND|REASON_APP_STANDBY` with `#netAvail=0` in a RARE bucket. Stopped, not deferred. Everything in §3.1 is chosen around this.

rows.name: The commute task body exercised by a test
rows.note: 10 tests, with the task callback captured at import and invoked against the real module. The gate cases were confirmed by removing the gate.

rows.name: Location timeline
rows.note: Sightings at named places, median last-seen per day, its own 28-day store. Silent for its first four days, by design.

rows.name: Call log, archive import
rows.note: Native build, and fatal for a store listing.

rows.name: Named places, location sharing, located answers
rows.note: Unverified since the fix that touched it.

rows.name: Weather and distance from measured figures
rows.note: The search provider is unverified, and a silent search failure looks exactly like hallucination. Routing is a public server that knows the road graph and not the road, so durations are free-flowing and the context says so.

rows.name: The situation sent to the persona
rows.note: Place, battery, link — one field. The highest character-per-line change available anywhere in the plan.

rows.name: Opening an app on the phone by name
rows.note: Confirmed twice over: by `topResumedActivity` and by the target app’s own launch event. Needed a native build.

rows.name: Governance: parked actions, approve and deny
rows.note: Desk actions only.

rows.name: Desk-watch countdown, silence locks
rows.note: The desk owns the clock; the phone’s countdown is a readout, never a decision timer. Do not move it.

rows.name: Scripts: list
Scripts: create, update, delete, run by id
rows.note: Which is why editing is disabled.

rows.name: Run history
rows.note: Reports currently invents “Last run: 2h ago” from a fixture.

rows.name: Presence — awake but idle
rows.note: Inferred from socket state today.

rows.name: Declared rules (“tell me if I haven’t…”)
rows.note: Spec written and awaiting review. Its presence half rests on a measurement that no longer holds.

rows.name: Anticipation v1 — noticed when you open the app
rows.note: Decided in code from the journal against its own baseline and the next departure. At most one a day, never the same subject twice running, silent by default.

rows.name: Anticipation that finds you in your pocket
rows.note: Needs the gateway push or a foreground service — the phone measurably cannot do it alone.

rows.name: Anticipation from learned habit rather than a written rule
rows.note: Needs the senses and weeks of baseline. Not shortenable by code.

rows.name: 19 screens, full suite and clean typecheck
rows.note: The number written in a doc goes stale — trust the run, not the comment.

rows.name: Standalone release APK, no bundler attached
Haptics, and an animation switch that works
OTA updates
rows.note: **Verified 2026-08-24.** Channel Active, branch linked, runtime matching the installed APK, latest group is HEAD. A **local** build still receives nothing unless the fingerprint is baked by hand — `prebuild` writes the literal placeholder and nothing logs a word about it.

rows.name: Contrast checked against WCAG AA
rows.note: 4.78 over the floor and 4.68 over the navy crown, against a bar of 4.5.

rows.name: A theme choice that did nothing — removed
rows.note: Dark and System were identical. A setting that does nothing is worse than an absent one.

rows.name: arm64-only build
rows.note: A config plugin, registered — so `prebuild` cannot silently revert it, which is this project’s most expensive recurring bug class. Roughly 35 MB against 100.7 MB across four ABIs. **The old ledger listed this as owed; it is done.**

rows.name: Motion defaulted from the OS
rows.note: Implemented at `src/theme/appearance.tsx:89` and spied on in a test; a deliberate toggle outranks it permanently. **The old ledger called this untested for want of code; it has code and a test, and owes only a device pass.**

rows.name: Light theme
rows.note: Broken by design — “System” behaves identically to Dark. Decide or remove.

rows.name: Appearance surviving a launch
rows.note: In-memory only. Accent, glow and motion all reset. The ledger claimed this for days.

rows.name: Crash and error reporting
rows.note: A native crash is silent — no red box, nothing an error boundary sees — so `adb logcat` on the one machine that built the APK is the only diagnosis. The JS half is shippable over the air; the native half needs a service and a build.

rows.name: A real release keystore
rows.note: Signed with Expo’s generated debug keystore, which is why a local APK and an EAS-signed one cannot replace each other.

rows.name: Screen-reader pass
rows.note: Targets are floored at 44–64px and roles are set; nothing has been checked with TalkBack.

rows.name: Tablet and landscape
rows.note: Locked to portrait. The reactor and the 2×2 grid need a breakpoint before a tablet is claimed.

queue.title: Confirm the OTA channel
queue.detail: Was one command and gated every JS-only fix behind it. Channel `production` is Active, the branch is linked, and the runtime matches the installed APK byte for byte — so a publish does reach the phone.

queue.title: The briefing-schedule row stops lying
queue.detail: A workspace-only week ages the upload stamp, and the panel then asserted the gateway lost the schedule — which the phone cannot know. Now three states: `AT THE GATEWAY`, `CANNOT TELL`, `ON THIS PHONE`. `cloudArmedState()` sits beside `cloudArmed()` rather than replacing it, so the task's gate is untouched and a stale stamp still means the phone posts. 10 new tests, and `tsc` caught a third call site the plan had missed.

queue.title: Provider effects that outlive their tree
queue.detail: An effect resolving after its test body corrupts the act environment, after which every later render returns an empty tree — no throw, no warning. It has cost six tests and is why the anti-duplicate wiring has none. Cancellation at the source, which the test file itself concluded was the real fix.

queue.title: A crash says what it was
queue.detail: Today a crash restarts in silence. The JS half is catchable, persistable and shippable now; a native crash still needs a service and a build, and stays owed rather than quietly folded in. The record is derived — no chat text, no token — because a crash log is exactly what gets pasted into a chat window.

queue.title: He answers out loud
queue.detail: Voice out is the largest single gap in the chat. The decision of whether and what to speak is pure and tested; the native call sits at the edge. Listening is a device check, not a change.

queue.title: He comes back after a reboot
queue.detail: Free, and the manifest has no `RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED` today. Goes in a config plugin, never in `android/` — that directory is regenerated and a hand edit reverts without saying so.

queue.title: The notification listener — spec and reducer only
queue.detail: The step change in presence: event-driven, nearly free, and more context than any polling. It is also gated by the token split, which is brain work. So the drop rules and the pure reducer get built and tested; no service is registered and no permission is asked. Data collected badly cannot be un-collected.

queue.title: Usable by someone who cannot see it well
queue.detail: Better than the old ledger admitted: contrast is measured and passing, and reduced motion already follows the OS. What is genuinely owed is a TalkBack pass.
